original_text: Types of Tissues Connective Tissue Specialized cells Ground substance -Noncellular material, fills space Protein fibers Collagen fibers -contain collagen providing strength and flexibility Reticular fibers  contain thinly branched collagen fibers Elastic fibers  contain elastin Categories include Fibrous, Supportive, & Fluid
explanation: Connective tissue binds and supports body parts. It is composed of three elements: specialized cells, an extracellular ground substance (a noncellular material that fills the space between cells), and protein fibers. The three types of protein fibers found in connective tissue matrix are: 1) Collagen fibers: provide structural strength and flexibility. 2) Reticular fibers: contain thin, highly branched collagen fibers that form supportive networks. 3) Elastic fibers: contain the protein elastin, allowing the tissue to stretch and recoil. Connective tissue is divided into three major categories: fibrous, supportive, and fluid.

questions.q: What are the three essential components of connective tissue?
opts: Specialized cells, ground substance, and protein fibers
questions.exp: Connective tissue is characterized by having specialized cells, an extracellular ground substance, and protein fibers.

questions.q: Which type of protein fiber provides stretch and recoil capabilities to connective tissues?
questions.exp: Elastic fibers contain the protein elastin, which allows them to stretch and recoil.
